classification.difficultyReason: Name consecutive vertices and explain a deliberately incorrect vertex order.

spec.description: Horizontal rectangle labelled A upper left, M upper right, K lower right, G lower left.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied labels visible; quadrilateral name withheld.

answer.short: $AMKG$ or $AGKM$; cyclic rotations are also valid.
answer.worked: Read consecutive vertices around the boundary: $A,M,K,G$ clockwise, or $A,G,K,M$ anticlockwise. Thus $AMKG$ or $AGKM$ is valid; either order may start at any vertex.

children.label: f
children.prompt:
Tommy was asked to draw a rectangle $ABCD$. This is what he sketched.
Explain why he is incorrect, and draw rectangle $ABCD$ correctly.

spec.sourceRegion: Label quadrilaterals, f, Tommy's supplied sketch
spec.description: Horizontal rectangle labelled A upper left, C upper right, D lower right and B lower left.
spec.mathematics: Boundary A–C–D–B–A deliberately differs from the requested consecutive order A–B–C–D.
spec.answerVisibility: Keep Tommy's incorrect labels visible and unchanged.

answer.short: The vertices are not in consecutive boundary order. One correct rectangle has $A$ upper left, $B$ lower left, $C$ lower right and $D$ upper right.
answer.worked: In Tommy's sketch, $B$ and $C$ are opposite vertices, so the order $A,B,C,D$ crosses the rectangle instead of following its boundary. Label consecutive vertices $A,B,C,D$ clockwise or anticlockwise. One correct drawing is shown.

spec.description: Correctly labelled rectangle with A upper left, B lower left, C lower right and D upper right.
spec.mathematics: A–B–C–D follows consecutive boundary vertices anticlockwise.
